name: TESSERA CORPONATION Bastion CorpSec Neural Fortress
description:
The Bastion CorpSec Neural Fortress is a Tier 4 security-hardened BCI engineered by TESSERA CORPONATION for deployment in elite corporate security divisions and executive protection units. Built around a triple-redundant AES-512 encryption core with quantum-resistant key rotation every 3.7 seconds, the Bastion integrates a dedicated threat-cognition co-processor that overlays real-time biometric threat assessment onto the wearer's visual field. Its neural architecture includes a hardware-level kill switch that renders all stored operational data irretrievable upon unauthorized access attempts, and a passive signal-dampening mesh that prevents remote interrogation of neural traffic. The installation footprint spans three cortical anchor points and requires a Class IV surgical suite with full neural mapping pre-operative workup.

Within TESSERA CORPONATION's internal security hierarchy, wearing a Bastion is a visible mark of rank—CorpSec personnel who have been issued one are informally referred to as 'Walled' by their peers, a term carrying equal parts respect and wariness. The unit's distinctive low-frequency carrier hum, barely perceptible to augmented hearing, has become something of a calling card in corporate espionage circles: rival operatives know that a 'Walled' target is nearly impossible to compromise neurologically. On the streets, decommissioned Bastions stripped from fallen CorpSec operatives command enormous black-market premiums, though most self-destruct before extraction is complete.

cultural_context: Within Meridian 88's corporate security ecosystem, the Bastion has transcended its functional role to become a cultural symbol of institutional loyalty and controlled lethality. TESSERA CORPONATION leverages this symbolism deliberately in internal recruiting materials, framing Bastion implantation as an initiation rite rather than a standard equipment issue. Critics within civil liberties organizations argue that the device's kill-switch and data-wipe capabilities represent a dangerous precedent for corporate control over employee cognition, a debate that has reached the Meridian 88 legislative floor twice without resolution.

story_hooks: A decommissioned Bastion surfaces on the black market still holding encrypted operational memory fragments—someone in TESSERA's upper hierarchy wants it back before its kill-switch timer expires, and they're not asking politely.

A CorpSec operative with a Bastion implant begins experiencing 'ghost overlay' artifacts that don't match any real biometric profiles—the images are of people who don't exist yet, or perhaps people who were erased.

A civil liberties attorney approaches the party after her client—a former TESSERA CorpSec agent—had their Bastion remotely wiped mid-trial, destroying the only neural evidence that could have proven a corporate war crime.
